interest: Hornbeck sidesteps consular friction over rules for American dentists in Japan.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
overview: This file (decimal 894.1282, running from September 1932 to June 1933) documents an inquiry by the U.S. Department of Commerce regarding the legal requirements and opportunities for American dentists to practice in Japan. Prompted by contradictory reports from American Consul Erle R. Dickover in Kobe and Consul General Arthur Garrels in Tokyo, the Department of State sought clarification. To prevent interpersonal friction between the two consular officers, the Division of Far Eastern Affairs privately instructed Counselor Edwin L. Neville at the Tokyo Embassy to investigate the matter directly with Japanese authorities. Following months of inquiries and personal visits to the Japanese Foreign Office, Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitted official regulations outlining examination and licensing procedures for foreign physicians and dentists, which the State Department then provided to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.
